sources.title: Fugu beta announcement
sources.evidence: April 24,2026 names Fugu Ultra and opens external beta applications. English describes API access and two available variants; Japanese says external beta begins but describes a planned lineup. This is limited beta opening, not unrestricted general availability.

sources.title: Fugu general availability
sources.evidence: June 22,2026 explicitly makes Fugu and Ultra generally available, after a beta with close to 500 users. Original Ultra coordinates worker models for multi-step tasks; no exact parameter count is published.

sources.title: Sakana Fugu Technical Report, section 3.2
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. Section 3.2 describes original Ultra as scaling the Conductor training approach from an unnamed pretrained regular language-model checkpoint, with GRPO and up to five workflow steps. It does not identify that checkpoint as the 7B research Conductor or name a Qwen version/size. Table 1 and Tables 2–4 report performance, not total or activated parameters; no nominal count is supplied.

sources.title: Original official integration catalog
sources.evidence: June 17 initial revision lists fugu-ultra, 1,000,000 context, text/image input, high reasoning, reasoning summaries and parallel tool calls. Client metadata establishes the interface profile, not public launch timing or a neural configuration.

sources.title: Current official versioned integration catalog
sources.evidence: Separately lists fugu-ultra-v1.0 with 1,000,000 context, text/image input, high/xhigh reasoning and parallel tools. Bare fugu-ultra is now displayed as v2.0, so that mutable entry is not used for original-version specifications.

sources.title: Sakana model identifiers and API contract
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. Explicitly maps fugu-ultra-v1.0 to fugu-ultra-20260615, while the bare fugu-ultra alias defaults to v2.0. This identifies the June snapshot, not its release day. API usage fields count orchestration tokens rather than neural parameters; neither total nor active parameters is reported.

sources.title: Gemma 4 orchestrator validation
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, including the benchmark and two-layer images. The August 10 note says previous Fugu orchestrators were Qwen-based, but supplies no Qwen version/size or exact original-Ultra checkpoint. Gemma 4 E2B is a separate backbone-interchangeability experiment. Similar-scale language and the plot of accuracy/cost do not identify original Ultra or give its total/active parameter count.

sources.title: Conductor research announcement
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. The April 27 announcement explicitly reports a 7B research Conductor and calls its research foundational to Fugu. It does not identify original production Ultra as that checkpoint or a size-preserving variant; the later Ultra report describes a newly trained, unnamed pretrained language-model checkpoint.

sources.title: Fugu Ultra v1.1 update
sources.evidence: July 24 introduces v1.1 and explicitly compares it with v1.0, adding newer worker models. This confirms distinct revisions, without revealing original Ultra parameter counts or topology.

sources.title: Fugu Max and Ultra v2 release
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. September 11 introduces distinct Max and Ultra v2 revisions and dates original Ultra v1 to June. The updated model pools and performance/cost comparisons do not identify an original Ultra backbone or supply its nominal total/active parameter counts.

sources.title: Sakana API Platform Terms of Service
sources.evidence: September 28 terms retain service/configuration intellectual property with Sakana and licensors and grant limited permission to use the service. API rights do not license model-weight redistribution.

sources.title: Official Fugu repository inventory
sources.evidence: Complete 435-entry public tree contains integration code/configuration, demos and research material, with no model checkpoint. A SakanaAI HuggingFace search for fugu returned no models. These checks supplement the explicit commercial API distribution.

sources.title: Later multi-agent self-supervision research
sources.evidence: October 12 article describes a separate 27B research experiment. It does not identify that model as the production Ultra orchestrator or provide missing original Ultra counts.

sources.title: Learning to Orchestrate Agents in Natural Language with the Conductor, sections 4.1 and A.1
sources.evidence: Freshly fetched October 27. Section 4.1 explicitly reports a 7B research Conductor, and Appendix A.1 names Qwen2.5-7B as its base. Its experiments use an older worker pool including Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4 and GPT-5. This is valid nominal evidence for that research checkpoint, but no original Ultra identity or unchanged-checkpoint link is stated; the benchmark tables do not establish an Ultra activated-parameter convention.

sources.title: Multi-Agent Self-Supervision, section 4.1 and comparison tables
sources.evidence: Freshly fetched October 27. Section 4.1 names Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 as the base of a separate MASS experiment using qwen-code. Tables compare MASS generations, supervision and evaluation outcomes; original Fugu Ultra is not a counted model row. The Fugu technical report appears as a reference, without identifying MASS as the production Ultra checkpoint or supplying any Ultra total/active count.

sources.title: Original Fugu launch benchmark table
sources.evidence: Freshly downloaded and visually inspected October 27. The Fugu Ultra column contains task scores across eleven benchmarks, with no parameter-size or activated-parameter row; it does not establish an active-count convention.

sources.title: Current Sakana Fugu product and research page
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. The page links TRINITY and Conductor as foundational research and labels its current quantitative results Fugu Ultra v2.0. It does not identify the original Ultra base checkpoint or publish total/active counts. Its current v2 results cannot be transferred to the original Ultra record.

sources.title: Secondary June 23 Fugu commentary claiming a 7B orchestrator
sources.evidence: Fresh search lead read October 27, not accepted as specification evidence. The article claims roughly 7B for Fugu, describes the older Conductor pool of Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4 and GPT-5, and links only the Fugu product/release pages. Those originals and the Ultra report do not assign 7B to original Ultra; no independent checkpoint evidence or activated-count convention is supplied.

name.note: Original named Ultra offering. Preserve its release history separately from the later v2 record; the current bare API alias is mutable.

developer.note: Sakana develops the learned orchestrator; worker models can come from other developers.

release_date.note: Earliest documented named-Ultra beta opening, limited to invited/applying testers. English says variants are available and Japanese announces external beta, while some wording is prospective. General availability followed June 22. The beta checkpoint is not explicitly equated to June v1.0;20260615 is a snapshot identifier, not independently verified release timing.

open_weights.note: Hosted commercial offering; no original Ultra checkpoint is distributed in the checked official public inventory. Public integration code and open worker models do not make the orchestrator open-weight.

license.note: Descriptive service classification, without transferring a worker license or the technical paper license to the complete model system.

parameters_b.note: October 27 re-audit found no published nominal total for original Ultra or a sufficiently identified base checkpoint from which to infer one. Qwen2.5-7B is the research Conductor; Gemma 4 E2B and Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 are separate experiments. Generic Qwen ancestry and a shared training method do not establish a named-model size lineage. A secondary 7B claim lacks that link; worker-pool sizes are not summed.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh original-paper, benchmark-image, later-research and version-documentation checks found no active-parameter count or stated counting convention for original Ultra. Tables report performance, cost or training outcomes. Workflow steps, selected workers and orchestration-token usage do not measure active neural weights; no dense-equals-active or summed-worker inference is made.

architecture.note: Neural backbone topology remains undisclosed. The supported system structure is a learned language-model orchestrator emitting worker/subtask/access-list workflows, trained with GRPO; it is not a neural MoE merely because multiple independent worker models participate. Historical Qwen lineage does not identify a dense/MoE variant.

context_window.note: Official original June client configuration and explicitly versioned v1.0 entry agree on 1,000,000 tokens. This is interface capacity, not proof of native router/worker training context or an April beta limit.

modalities.note: Original and v1.0 interface metadata support text/image inputs; the composed service returns textual answers or function arguments. This does not establish an image encoder in the orchestrator itself.

reasoning.note: Original June interface supports high reasoning and summaries; explicit v1.0 metadata later supports high/xhigh. Reasoning capability describes the composed service, without assuming current v2 behavior.

tool_call.note: Original report explicitly implements model-selected agent function calls and their routing; both original and v1.0 catalogs support parallel tool calls.

description.value: Language-model orchestrator trained with reinforcement learning to compose multi-step workflows across a pool of worker models.
description.note: Specific to original Ultra workflow construction, including selected workers, subtasks and communication topology; avoids transferring the single-worker Fugu router or later v2 results.

patch.description: Language-model orchestrator trained with reinforcement learning to compose multi-step workflows across a pool of worker models.

patch.notes: April 24,2026 marks the named Fugu Ultra beta opening with application/invitation limits; June 22 was general availability. Exact beta-to-June checkpoint continuity is not documented. This record preserves the original release; current fugu-ultra defaults to v2.0, while original v1.0 is also known as fugu-ultra-20260615. The date inside that identifier does not establish release timing. Original June and explicitly versioned v1.0 metadata support 1,000,000 context, text/image inputs, reasoning and tools as service capabilities. Ultra learns worker/subtask/communication workflows with GRPO, isolating tool trajectories within each workflow and sharing history across workflows. Total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed. The original Ultra base checkpoint is unnamed; Qwen2.5-7B Conductor, Gemma 4 E2B and Qwen3.6-27B MASS are separate research models, with no documented size lineage to original Ultra. Neural topology also remains undisclosed. No authenticated inference request was made.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit preserves both counts as undisclosed after reopening original Ultra training/version sources, inspecting benchmark images, tracing named Conductor and MASS backbones, and bounded fresh searches for nominal and activated counts. No sufficiently identified original-Ultra base lineage or later original comparison count was found; the secondary 7B claim does not establish that identity. Adds explicit null parameter patches and preserves the other twelve field assessments, including original release/version distinctions.
